newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece renews effort to get back Parthenon marbles.
newsitem.headline: Greece renews effort to get back Parthenon marbles.

text.p: Greece will launch a new campaign to reclaim the Parthenon marbles from the British Museum in London, Prime Minister Costas Simitis said on Wednesday.

The return of the classical sculptures known in England as the Elgin marbles has been a long-standing Greek demand, first put to the British government by the late actress and culture minister Melina Mercouri.

"The political and legal procedure for claiming the Parthenon marbles has been launched," Simitis told reporters. "Our target is to finish the first phase and present the issue to the European Union by December."
The request was put anew before the British government on October 25 during a meeting between the British ambassador in Athens and Culture Minister Evangelos Venizelos, he said.
Lord Elgin, a British diplomat, removed the friezes from the top of the classical temple in 1806 with permission from the local Ottoman Turkish administrators.
Those who resist the return of the marbles to Greece say the British Museum safeguarded them from damage while other sculptures at the Acropolis temples suffered Athens' notorious air pollution.
Greece has said it will build a museum at the foot of the Acropolis hill to house them. A design contest was held but construction never began due to protests from local residents.
Simitis said a contract with the museum's Italian architects will be signed next month and the building will be finished in three years.
